messages:
jonah: heads up — nightly evals on model v2q-2026-03 showed a big entropy spike starting 03:00 UTC, lots of prompt-set failures. tagging @sophia and @maria to triage.
sophia: saw that in the dashboard, esp on the summarization prompts. BLEU/ROUGE dropped and outputs got repetitive but with very high token logprobs? weird.
maria: can you paste the eval excerpt? also which runner and quantization profile did this run use?
jonah: run metadata — runner: redwood-runtime-rtg-2, quant: fp16->q4_0, sampling: temp=0.7 top_p=0.95 top_k=50 seed=auto, batch=8. eval-bot attached the snippet below.
eval-bot: automated report:
```
EVAL RUN 2026-03-19T03:00Z
model: v2q-2026-03
quant_profile: q4_0
sampling: temp=0.7 top_p=0.95 top_k=50 seed=auto
metric_summary:
 - rougeL: -12.4% (regression)
 - accuracy: -9.8%
entropy_mean: 6.2 -> 9.7 (spike)
perplexity: 18.3 -> 45.1
note: distribution shift at token positions 3-8
```
kevin: seed=auto means RNG state seeded by time; if some worker had bad RNG initialization it could bias sampling. we saw similar once when a batch reused the same prng stream across tokens.
sophia: good call. Maria, any recent runtime patch that touches RNG/kv cache ordering? we landed a kv-cache reorder PR last week for memory packing.
maria: yes PR#3421 touched kv flush ordering but shouldn't affect RNG. however, there was a small change in the worker bootstrap that altered how we seed per-worker. it defaulted to `std::random_device()` -> entropy pool; I added a fallback that used pid+time for containers with no entropy. could be nondeterministic across runs.
jonah: interesting — that fallback could produce correlated seeds across replicas if time resolution coarse. ops-bot, did we have any node restarts around 02:59-03:01 UTC in the pool?
ops-bot: cluster events:
 - 2026-03-19T02:58:47Z node c-12 restarted (OOM remediation)
 - 2026-03-19T02:59:03Z autoscaler spun up worker c-27
 - 2026-03-19T03:00:12Z model server restarted on c-27
sophia: that lines up. new worker might have used fallback seeding and replicated stream across requests. if many requests used same RNG seed we could see reduced sampling entropy and odd token concentration.
kevin: reduced entropy usually lowers diversity, not spike. but logs show entropy increased. hypothesis: duplicated seed + quantization numerical noise -> unstable logits magnitude -> higher softmax entropy intermittently.
jonah: I pulled a per-request log from 03:00:22Z — showing repeated top token probs around 0.05-0.1 and lots of near-uniform distributions. snippet:
```
REQUEST 03:00:22Z id=rr-91
logits_sample:
 - token 0: 0.12
 - token 1: 0.11
 - token 2: 0.10
 - ... many tokens ~0.03-0.06
sampled_token: 42
```
maria: that pattern feels like quantization saturation. q4_0 has known mid-range step issues with tiny logits being flattened. combined with correlated RNG it might flip sampling behavior unpredictably.
sophia: action items: (1) re-run nightly with fixed deterministic seed per-eval (seed=42) to see if regression persists, (2) re-run with fp16 (no quant) to isolate quant effect, (3) add per-worker unique seed at bootstrap using our KDF from HSM to avoid time-based collisions.
kevin: I'll schedule quick re-runs. also suggest adding an eval-level check: compute per-request seed hash and detect duplicates across replicas; fail early if duplicates found.
jonah: started re-run job r-180912-1 with seed=42, same model/runner/quant. queued.
(5m later)
eval-bot: r-180912-1 completed.
```
EVAL RUN r-180912-1
sampling: seed=42
metric_summary:
 - rougeL: -0.9% (within noise)
 - accuracy: -0.6%
entropy_mean: 6.2 -> 6.4 (no spike)
```
sophia: ok seed=42 eliminated the spike. now re-run with no-quant (fp16) but seed=auto to test quant effect.
jonah: started r-180912-2 (fp16, seed=auto)
(10m later)
eval-bot: r-180912-2 completed.
```
EVAL RUN r-180912-2
quant_profile: fp16
sampling: seed=auto
metric_summary:
 - rougeL: -1.1% (small)
entropy_mean: 6.3
```
maria: looks like quant was the main factor — when fp16, entropy stable even with seed=auto. so combined factors: q4_0 numerical artifacts + fallback seeding on new workers produced the large spike.
kevin: recommended fixes:
 - revert fallback seeding to use secure KDF per worker (deploy next patch)
 - add a guard in runtime to detect low-variance RNG across batch and log at warn level
 - schedule a quant-sensitivity test in CI for q4_0 on long context runs
sophia: agreed. I'll open issues for each and assign owners. Jonah, can you roll the revert to staging? tag me when deployed so we can monitor tomorrow's nightly.
jonah: will roll revert and seed KDF to staging in the next 30m. will add a temporary eval that runs every hour on a small prompt set to catch regressions faster.
maria: also documenting this in the onboarding notes for quantized models: add a bullet about RNG seeding interactions with quant noise.
jonah: thanks all. closing triage thread — will repost if we see recurrence. :thumbsup:
